rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window for all 10 compounds and identify critical pairs. Starting at low organic minimizes early co-elution, while the high final organic and remaining hold time reduce the risk of missing retained compounds.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how the closest pairs respond to gradient steepness. The scouting run has substantial resolution margin, so a faster gradient may retain full resolution.

Test an intermediate slope to recover the strongly slope-sensitive central separation without returning to the long scouting run. This will locate the resolution–time tradeoff before adjusting temperature for selectivity.

Keep the near-optimal slope and raise temperature to test selectivity of the remaining critical pair. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving room to use a shallower gradient if needed.

The central pair appears to have reversed elution order between 40 and 50 C; a further temperature increase may separate it again. At 55 C, the neighboring gaps should still provide useful clearance while the last peak remains within the zero-time-penalty region.

Slightly steepen the gradient at 55 C to increase separation of the temperature-reversed critical pair while preserving the neighboring pair's resolution margin. The final organic fraction remains well above the observed elution window, and the shorter gradient should retain the zero time penalty.

Increase the slope by one final-organic grid step to nudge the critical pair above R = 1.5. The neighboring pair still has resolution margin, and the faster elution should preserve the zero time penalty.

The maximum CRF has been reached; retain injection 7 as the best method. Test one more slope increment for a slightly larger critical-pair resolution margin and shorter retention while aiming to preserve the maximum score.

With the maximum CRF already secured, test a modest increase in starting organic to shorten retention and assess selectivity around the two closest pairs. The first peak remains sufficiently retained in injection 8 to justify this small window shift.

Reduce the slope at the higher starting organic to restore the newly limiting pair while retaining the improved separation of the other central pair. This tests whether a shifted, narrower gradient window provides more resolution margin at the maximum CRF.

Test a further shifted, narrower window to improve the minimum resolution while preserving the maximum CRF already achieved. The shallower slope should offset the loss of separation caused by raising starting organic, and the final organic remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction.

Lower the final organic by one grid step to recover resolution of the limiting pair in injection 11. This modest slope reduction should keep the last peak within the zero-time-penalty region while testing for a larger resolution margin at CRF 1.000.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 12 to balance its two closest separations and potentially increase the minimum resolution. The estimated last-peak elution fraction is about 0.54, so a 0.60 endpoint should still elute all compounds during the gradient without a time penalty.

With the maximum score secured, explore a hotter, shallower-gradient alternative for greater resolution margin. The longer gradient should counter compression of the earlier central pair at higher temperature, while 60 C may keep the last peak within the zero-time-penalty region.

Return to the best-resolution maximum-score region and make the slope slightly shallower than injection 13 to balance its two limiting pairs near R = 1.7. The higher endpoint keeps the last compound safely inside the gradient, with expected retention still below 10 minutes.

Test a slightly shallower, trimmed gradient near injection 10, aiming to preserve CRF 1.000 with more resolution margin than the fastest successful method. The 0.70 endpoint remains comfortably above the estimated last-peak elution fraction.

Test a lower-temperature alternative to the maximum-score methods at 55 C. Relative to injection 3, the shallower slope should improve the central separation, while the higher starting organic may offset the added retention time.

Raise starting organic one step to bring the last peak below 10 minutes and remove injection 17's small time penalty. The accompanying slope reduction may help preserve full resolution, yielding a maximum-score alternative at 40 C.

Refine the successful 40 C method with a higher starting organic and narrower window. The shallower slope may increase central-pair resolution while the higher starting organic offsets retention time; monitor the first pair for excessive compression.

Slightly reduce the slope relative to injection 19 to improve its marginal central-pair resolution. The predicted last-peak retention remains below 10 minutes, so this refinement may preserve maximum CRF with a larger separation margin.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a cooler alternative that may improve the central critical pair's selectivity. Use a slightly steeper gradient than injection 19 to offset increased retention, while checking whether another central pair becomes limiting.

Return to the successful 40 C region and slightly flatten the slope relative to injection 20 to improve its limiting separation. The last peak is expected just below 10 minutes, preserving maximum CRF, and the endpoint remains above its estimated elution fraction.

Refine the faster maximum-score region with a slope between injections 9 and 10, aiming to balance the two limiting pairs while shortening retention. This should preserve full resolution and the zero time penalty without repeating a previous method.

Refine around injection 15, which achieved maximum CRF with the largest observed minimum resolution. This slightly shallower gradient should retain approximately R = 1.7 for both critical pairs while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Use the final injection to test a slightly faster gradient within the established maximum-score region at 55 C. Relative to injection 12, the small slope increase should shorten retention while retaining resolution above 1.5 for both critical pairs; CRF 1.000 is already secured.
